title: Low Altitude Air Defense Officer (I) (Capt to 2ndLt) PMOS, DC AVN
raw_text:
2. MOS 7204, Low Altitude Air Defense Officer (I) (Capt to 2ndLt) PMOS, DC
AVN

    a. Summary. Low Altitude Air Defense (LAAD) Officers serve as
commanders or staff officers within ground based air defense (GBAD) units,
with the mission of providing surface to air fires in defense of Marine air
ground task force critical assets from threat unmanned aerial systems,
missiles, and fixed and rotary wing aircraft. They coordinate tactical


                                          1-261                        Enclosure (1)
 1141                                                                  NAVMC 1200.1L



employment of LAAD units through air command and control agencies, sensors,
and other air defense weapons. They evaluate intelligence, plan surface to
air fires at all echelons, and direct administration, communication, supply,
maintenance, and security activities of LAAD units. LAAD Officers also plan
tactical employment and command LAAD units conducting airbase ground security
operations. The Joint Air Operations Center Air Command and Control Course
(JAOC2C) (F19L2W2), JT-101 Introduction to Multi-Tactical Data Link Network
Operations Course (JT-101 Intro to MTN OPS) (JKO), JT-102 Multi-TDL Advanced
Joint Interoperability Course (JT-102 MAJIC) (A05L6Z1), JT-201 Multi-TDL
Network Planners Course (A05KHY1), Antiterrorism Officer Level II Course,
MAWTS-1 LAAD Enhancement Training Instructor (LETI) Course, and the MAWTS-1
Weapons and Tactics Instructor (WTI) Course (M149731) are available as
skills enhancement training for the Low Altitude Air Defense Officer.

       b.   Prerequisites

            (1) At least 64 inches in height.

            (2) Must have normal color perception.

            (3) Security requirement:     secret security clearance eligibility.

            (4) Hearing loss no greater than 15 dB between 500 Hz and 2000 Hz.

        (5) Must have 20/20 vision (may be correctable to 20/20 with
eyeglasses or contact lenses).

        (6) Must meet MOS classification standards, as listed in the glossary
(pg. xiv) prior to graduating from the Basic School.

    c. Requirements. Complete the Aviation Command and Control Commons
Course (M09C2A1) and the Low Altitude Air Defense (LAAD) Basic Officer Course
(M09ANS1) at Marine Corps Air Ground Combat Center (MCAGCC) at Twentynine
Palms, CA.

    d. Duties. For a complete listing of duties and tasks, refer to
reference (ag), Aviation Training and Readiness (T&R) Manual, Low Altitude
Air Defense.

    e. Related Standard Occupational Classification (SOC) Title and Code.
Artillery and Missile Officers 55-1014.

       f.   Related Military Skill.     None.

nlx_method: NLx employer-demand profiles; private-only ownership unverified. Six-digit profiles pool specialty weighted task incidences after the existing review exclusion mask and five-job task-support floor; destination SOCs require 200 postings and nonzero tasks. Military profiles use binary accepted task presence and the same NLx reference RCA weights as civilian profiles: reciprocal positive task shares (zero weight for reference-absent tasks) of pooled retained support-five NLx weighted incidences across 1,016 reference specialties (912 eligible comparison candidates), sqrt(q * rca_weight), then L2 normalization and cosine. No military crosswalk codes enter the task ranking. All positive top-20 results retained; zero-similarity destinations are not recommendations. Shared field/rating duties are included; general Naval Standards remain separate by paygrade. Summary compares non-future individual source entries (versions can repeat) with nonempty reference sets; grouped, future and general-standard entries remain in all outputs. Hit@k is the fraction with at least one reference SOC recovered; ties are averaged exactly. References outside NLx remain in denominators. DMDC reference status is from July 2024, not current 2026 status.
